name: device-cdac-cap
description: CDAC unit-capacitor characterization: MiM (2.0 / 1.5 / 1.0 fF/um^2) effective density vs unit size, voltage coefficient and temperature coefficient, plus the 3.3 V MOS cap as the contrast case, over the cap corners.
claim: None yet — device characterization ahead of a ratified spec line (#1). Feeds #8 (CDAC unit-cap sizing) and #14 (Monte Carlo calibration). Also the harness's proof that the mimcap/moscap .lib sections take effect, which no MOS-only corner sweep can show.

cmim_2f0_ff.description: 10x10 um MiM at 2.0 fF/um^2 is ~200 fF plus perimeter. The process floor proves the mimcap_ff/mimcap_ss sections are actually selected — the guard a MOS-only sweep cannot provide.

cmim_1f0_ff.description: same geometry at 1.0 fF/um^2. Independent confirmation the MiM corner params reach both density flavors.

cmim_1f5_ff.description: same geometry at 1.5 fF/um^2, the third flavor the PDK ships. Its corner multiplier is a separate model parameter (mim_corner_1p5fF), so this is a third independent confirmation the mimcap sections reach every flavor.

cmos_ff.description: 3.3 V NMOS cap biased at vdd. The process floor proves moscap_ff/moscap_ss take effect. (The supply floor this check carried before the #4 extension is dropped: the model's C(V) tanh is fully saturated above ~0.7 V, so 2.97-3.63 V moves it by 0 %, and the voltage coefficient is now measured properly by cmos_vcc_ppm_v across 0 -> 3.3 V instead.)

cmim_density_ratio.description: the 2.0 fF/um^2 flavor holds ~2x the 1.0 fF/um^2 flavor at equal area; a sanity check that both aliases resolve to different models.

dens_2f0_2u.description: effective density of a 2x2 um unit cap. Perimeter fringe (c_capsw) is a LARGER fraction of a small unit, so the effective density is ABOVE the nominal 1.99 fF/um^2 plate density — the opposite of the intuition that a small cap loses density. #8 needs this to convert a unit-cap area budget into fF. Bounds allow for the PDK's +/-10 % mimcap process corners on top of the nominal plate+fringe value.

dens_2f0_20u.description: effective density of a 20x20 um unit cap, where perimeter fringe is a small correction. Together with dens_2f0_2u this brackets the plate-vs-fringe split across the plausible unit-cap range. Bounds allow for the PDK's +/-10 % mimcap process corners on top of the nominal plate+fringe value.

cmim_2f0_vcc_ppm_v.description: FINDING, asserted as a check: the simulated MiM cap has EXACTLY ZERO voltage coefficient. The gf180mcu model card defines c_vcr1/c_vcr2 for every MiM flavor, but sm141064_mim.ngspice comments out the bias-dependent `c_cap` line and instantiates a fixed `.MODEL C cap=c_c0`. Any simulated CDAC linearity result therefore contains no MiM voltage-coefficient contribution. This check is deliberately tight so that a future PDK revision wiring c_vcr* into the deck fails loudly here rather than silently changing every CDAC record.

cmos_vcc_ppm_v.description: the contrast case: the 3.3 V MOS cap's C(V) is a tanh, so its 0 -> 3.3 V voltage coefficient is enormous (order 1e7 ppm/V, i.e. tens of x, not ppm). This is the quantitative reason a MOS cap is not a CDAC unit element.

tc_2f0_ppm_k.description: temperature coefficient of the 2.0 fF/um^2 MiM over -40 -> 125 C, measured inside every deck via per-instance dtemp. The model card gives tc1 = 1.46e-5 /K and tc2 = -5.55e-8 /K^2, which integrate to 12.66 ppm/K over this span; the band is that value +/-25 %. The process ceiling asserts what a tempco must be: a RATIO, so the mimcap corner multiplier (a scale factor on C) has to cancel out of it.

tc_1f0_ppm_k.description: same for the 1.0 fF/um^2 flavor (tc1 = 1.302e-5, tc2 = -4.93e-9 -> 12.85 ppm/K). It lands within 2 % of the 2.0 fF/um^2 flavor, so a flavor change is not a tempco change.

tc_1f5_ppm_k.description: and for the 1.5 fF/um^2 flavor, whose tc1 = 4.06e-5 is 2.8x the other two (-> 38.2 ppm/K). This is a real selection input for #8: the middle-density flavor is the WORST of the three thermally, which is not something one would guess.

tc_mos_ppm_k.description: FINDING, asserted as a check: the 3.3 V MOS cap has NO modelled temperature dependence whatsoever. Its subckt accepts dtemp and forwards it to a behavioural capacitor whose C(V) expression contains no temperature term, so -40 C and 125 C read identically. A flat temperature column could be a plumbing failure; this null control is what makes it a statement about the model.

evidence.data_provenance: simulated — gf180mcu ngspice device models (sm141064_mim.ngspice cap_mim_new, sm141064.ngspice moscap), swept over the PDK's own mimcap/moscap corner sections. No foundry datasheet or literature value is involved. The datasheet-only parameters that are NOT in the simulated path (c_vcr1/c_vcr2) are tabulated in sim/device-characterization-report.md and flagged there as model-card values, not measurements.
notes: Effective C is derived from a 1 A AC probe at 1 MHz: C = 1/(2*pi*f*|V|). It is a small-signal capacitance at the stated bias, not a large-signal charge-transfer capacitance.

The open gf180mcu PDK ships no MoM / lateral-flux capacitor model, so no MoM corner is swept here; a MoM-based CDAC would need parasitic extraction rather than a model corner. Audited reproducibly by sim/tools/pdk_mismatch_audit.py (finding `mom-capacitor-model`).

MATCHING: the PDK provides NO local (device-to-device) mismatch data for any capacitor. Its `mimcap_statistical` section defines only mc_c_cox_* gated on sw_stat_global — a die-global multiplier that cancels in a capacitor ratio and therefore contributes nothing to CDAC DNL/INL. sigma(dC/C) for the unit cap is consequently NOT obtainable from this PDK; see sim/device-characterization-report.md for the literature-based assumption and derating used instead, and sim/tools/pdk_mismatch_audit.py (finding `cap-local-mismatch`) for the reproducible audit behind this statement.

VOLTAGE COEFFICIENT: the MiM model card carries c_vcr1/c_vcr2 but the ngspice deck does not apply them (the bias-dependent c_cap line is commented out in sm141064_mim.ngspice). cmim_2f0_vcc_ppm_v measures what the simulator does — zero. Note also that the 2.0 fF/um^2 card makes c_vcr1 GEOMETRY-dependent (+8.742e-6 /V for a plate over 5 um, -81e-6 /V at or below 5 um): the small unit caps a 10-bit array wants carry a ~9x larger, opposite-sign datasheet VCC than the 10x10 um device measured here. Neither value is in the simulated path.

TEMPERATURE COEFFICIENT is measured inside each deck by pinning three instances of each MiM flavor to absolute -40 / 27 / 125 C with a per-instance dtemp offset, rather than by differencing three rows of the grid. That makes it a checked quantity at every one of the 63 PVT points. The grid's own temperature axis is the independent cross-check and agrees.

Testbench extended 2026-07-31 for #4: branches 1-3 (cmim_2f0_ff, cmim_1f0_ff, cmos_ff, cmim_density_ratio) are unchanged in topology and remain comparable with record 20260731-155428-860c970, EXCEPT that every AC probe node gained an explicit 1 T DC return path. That is a bug fix, not a cosmetic change: without it the deck was singular at DC, fell back to a transient operating point, and reported the MOS cap at a partially-charged bias (224.556 fF where the model gives 398.3 fF). This record supersedes 20260731-155428-860c970 for the cmos_ff claim; the MiM columns are unaffected to every printed digit.
